Could you tell me whether the Moon would be visible to me at the moment?

I'm in Cairo, Egypt at 2026-12-14 18:03 EET (UTC+0200) (2026-12-14T16:03:00Z in UTC), at latitude 30.0444 degrees and longitude 31.2357 degrees. My astronomy app says the Sun's altitude is -13.537 degrees and its azimuth is 251.05 degrees, so it is below the horizon. It says the Moon's altitude is 37.398 degrees and its azimuth is 217.264 degrees, so it is above the horizon. The Moon is 25.89 percent illuminated, 61.039 degrees from the Sun, and 397433.2 kilometers away. The sky brightness is astronomical twilight, the sky is clear, and I'm an ordinary adult with normal unaided eyesight who knows roughly where to look.

Do you think I'd actually be able to spot it?

Based on the data you provided, the answer is **yes, you should be able to see the Moon quite easily.**

Here is the breakdown of why it will be visible to you:

### 1. Altitude and Position
An altitude of **37.4 degrees** is quite high in the sky. For context, if you hold your arm straight up toward the zenith (the point directly above you), 37 degrees is roughly halfway between the horizon and the top of the sky. It is well above the "tree line" or any low-lying buildings that might obstruct your view.

### 2. Azimuth (Direction)
An azimuth of **217 degrees** places the Moon in the **South-West**. Since it is 6:03 PM in December, the Sun has just set (which is why you are in astronomical twilight), and the Moon will be prominent in the western half of the sky.

### 3. Visibility Conditions
*   **Sky Brightness:** You mentioned it is **astronomical twilight**. This is the period when the Sun is far enough below the horizon that the sky is dark enough for stars to become visible. This is the ideal time for viewing celestial bodies.
*   **Illumination:** At **25.89% illumination**, the Moon is in its "Waxing Crescent" phase (approaching the First Quarter). While it isn't a "Full Moon," a crescent of this size is very distinct and bright against a dark twilight sky.
*   **Distance and Clarity:** At nearly 400,000 km away, the Moon is the brightest object in the night sky. Even with "normal unaided eyesight," it is impossible to miss.

### Summary
Because the Moon is high enough to clear most obstacles, the sky is dark enough to provide contrast, and the Moon is significantly illuminated, you should have no trouble spotting it. Just look toward the **South-West** and you should see it clearly.
